newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Comalco NZ to hit full post-upgrade capacity in 97.
newsitem.headline: Comalco NZ to hit full post-upgrade capacity in 97.

text.p: Comalco New Zealand Ltd will reach full capacity of 313,000 tonnes a year at its Tiwai Point aluminium smelter in the middle of 1997, a company spokeswoman said on Monday.
"The 313,000 is due to be reached in the middle of the year...They're ramping up to meeting that target," she said.
Comalco NZ, a unit of Comalco Ltd, owns 79.36 percent of the Tiwai Point smelter in the South Island and Sumitomo Chemical Company of Japan holds a 20.64 percent interest.
The upgrade has cost NZ$465 million and will increase capacity from 270,000 tonnes previously.
Comalco said earlier it was targeting further cost reductions at Tiwai Point and was looking to cut some jobs in the support and service areas.

A statement said the company's performance had suffered recently from higher input costs and a much stronger New Zealand dollar. It had also been dealing with cost increases associated with the commissioning of the upgrade.
The spokeswoman said Tiwai Point employs 1,180 people, of whom more than 300 are in support and service. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
